title: Henkin semantics: relation domains and comprehension
summary: Restrict relation quantifiers, express comprehension, and recover completeness and compactness through an exact first-order translation.
abstract: A second-order quantifier can range over a chosen family of relations instead of every relation on the domain. What must that family contain? Comprehension asks it to contain the relations described by specified formulas, while still leaving room for externally missing subsets. Treating available relations as another kind of object turns these structures into ordinary first-order models. We prove the model correspondence in both directions, recover completeness and compactness for a precise translated calculus, and explain why even full comprehension permits nonstandard arithmetic.
